items.title: Luther Henderson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Lena Horne evidently needed an arranger and music conductor and Ellington and Strayhorn who were very friendly with her suggested me. So anyway, I became, I went with, she came to my studio and we, she, I played something with her and so forth and she seemed to like it and all. Then we got together.

ctx.x: Okay. Now I had been a few years away from Lena Horne because I was with her in late '40s, maybe '50s, something like that. Anyway, the Symphony of the Air, Don Gillis had, I don't know, been commissioned that he was to do these works which he was already doing with his band. I don't know if he was doing Night Creature. I think Night Creature may have been done specifically for that concert. But at any rate, and he wanted to perform it at Carnegie Hall with a, in a symphony setting. And this is when he called me…

his band thing was, where he was gonna play that night, and then after the gig is over, you go and get something to eat and somehow he would stay up and he would talk and play .. I have some little cassettes about how he would instruct us, what he wanted to do and stuff like that. So it came like that.
